description: Somos un equipo de 6 desarrolladoras full-stack altamente motivadas y enfocadas en el trabajo colaborativo. Nuestra meta es clara: ganar el NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Estamos participando en el desafío "La Máquina de Discos de Información de la Tierra" (Earth Jukebox), donde buscamos transformar las complejas visualizaciones de datos de la NASA en experiencias de sonido interactivas y accesibles.

Mission: The Earth Information Jukebox
SONARIA is an interactive geographic sonification platform that transforms NASA scientific visualizations into auditory experiences, enabling users to explore and interpret information about our planet beyond sight.
By analyzing imagery from NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC), the system identifies visual features such as colors, intensities, and spatial patterns, translating them into sound parameters including pitch, rhythm, and tone. This allows users to explore maps and discover how different environmental phenomena are represented through sound.
The platform features ARIA, a virtual assistant inspired by topographic contours and sound waves, who guides users through the exploration process and helps them interpret scientific information.
SONARIA addresses the Earth Information Jukebox challenge by combining science, technology, and accessibility. It aims to reduce barriers faced by blind and low-vision individuals when accessing geographic and environmental information, while promoting a more inclusive and multisensory way of understanding our changing planet.
details: Sonaria is an accessible web application that transforms NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC) satellite maps into an interactive auditory experience for visually impaired users. It uses a custom Web Audio API engine to read map colors in real-time and translate them into musical instruments, guided by "Aria," a voice assistant built with the Web Speech API. Users press the Spacebar to select from three maps (Aerosols, Chlorophyll, and CO2), then navigate using keyboard arrows or voice commands (e.g., saying "Go to Bolivia" instantly relocates the cursor). Color intensity dictates pitch—vibrant colors produce high notes, while opaque colors produce low, deep sounds. The project's creativity lies in its "semantic sonification," applying artistic rules to assign specific instruments to scientific data rather than generating chaotic noise. Our team prioritized universal accessibility, scientific rigor by exclusively using official NASA datasets, and zero-latency performance by avoiding heavy third-party audio libraries, ultimately aiming to democratize Earth science and climate data for everyone.
